prompt: Sort entries by group number ONLY and return their names, relying on the stability of Java's list sort to keep insertion order inside each group. Complete namesGroupedStable, then run the tests.
explanation: List.sort (and Collections.sort) is guaranteed to be stable: elements that compare as equal keep their relative input order. That means a comparator that looks ONLY at the group number is enough to cluster the groups while preserving arrival order within each group -- adding a name comparison would actually break the required behavior. Sorting a copy leaves the caller's list untouched.
hints: Copy the input with new ArrayList<>(entries) so you can sort freely.
Sort with java.util.Comparator.comparingInt(Entry::group) and nothing else -- stability handles the rest.
After sorting, loop over the entries and collect e.name() into a new list of strings.
